chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah! I have encountered severe distress from the insinuations of the chest, and I am a man in debt, with dependents, and in need.'

So he said to him, 'Repeat these words: I rely upon the Living Who does not die, and the praise is for Allah Who did not take a companion nor a son, and there was not for Him an associate in the dominion, and there was not for Him a guardian from the disgrace, and exalt Him with Takbeer.'

'I rely upon the Living Who does not die, and the praise is for Allah Who did not take a companion nor a son, and there was not for Him an associate in the dominion, and there was not for Him a guardian from the disgrace, and exalt Him with Takbeer.'
And he did not long before he came to him and said, 'Allah removed the insinuations of my chest from me, and settled my debt for me, and expanded my sustenance for me.'

key_terms.الْحَيِّ الَّذِي لَا يَمُوتُ: The Living Who does not die

ai.seo_question: What supplication did the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) prescribe for relieving debt and chest insinuations?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith highlights the therapeutic power of specific dhikr in alleviating both spiritual anxiety (waswasa) and material hardship, a practice emphasized in Shia tradition for its holistic benefit. The Prophet’s instruction to repeat the declaration of Allah as 'the Living who does not die' underscores the reliance on Divine permanence to counter human transience and need. This narrative serves as a practical model for integrating spiritual remembrance with the resolution of worldly debts and distress.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Hamza Al Sumaly, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘A man came over to the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> and he said, ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! I am facing intense Satanic insinuations of the chest, and I am a man in debts, with dependants, needy’.

So hesaww said: ‘Reiterate these words, ‘I rely upon the Living Who will no be dying, and the Praise is for Allahazwj Who neither Took a female companion nor a son, and there does not happen to be an associate for Himazwj in the Kingdom, and there does not happen to be a guardian for Himazwj from the disgrace, and I exclaim Hisazwj Greatness with Takbeer’’.

So it was not long before he came over to him<sup>saww</sup> and he said, ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Removed the Satanic insinuations of my chest and Fulfilled my debts from me and Expanded my sustenance upon me’’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Muskan from abu Hamza al-Thumali from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:
“Once a man came to the Holy Prophet and said, ‘O Messenger of Allah, I face a strong insinuation in my chest (mind) and I am a man with a family, indebted and needy.’

The Messenger of Allah told him to repeat these words: ‘I place my trust in the Living One, Who does not die, all praise belongs to Allah, Who has not taken any companion, or children. Who has no partner in His Kingdom, and no guardian against defeat and you must say that He is greater than can be described.’
Shortly thereafter he came and said, ‘Allah has removed the insinuation from my chest, enabled me to pay my debts and has increased my sustenance.’”
